observations.behavior: Adds a new helper method to generate aliases like __join_1, __join_2 by inspecting the join chain and reserving names against existing table aliases.
observations.posthog_connection: ClickHouse HogQL execution may require explicit aliases for subqueries or joins; this could prevent query failures when alias collisions occur.

observations.behavior: Changes conditional logic so that non-USING joins also receive an alias before visiting their children. This unifies alias assignment across different join types.
observations.posthog_connection: Could resolve cases where ClickHouse rejected queries with missing aliases on standard JOINs rather than only USING-style constraints.

observations.behavior: Adds tests checking that generated aliases are present and do not collide with user-supplied aliases in chained cross-joins.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection but does not independently establish production benefit without runtime behavior evidence.

observations.limitations: Only test assertions and resolver changes are shown; no database compatibility checks, migration notes, or release configuration indicating whether this fixes actual customer-reported errors.

review.limitations: Only test assertions and resolver changes are shown; no database compatibility checks, migration notes, or release configuration indicating whether this fixes actual customer-reported errors.
review.reason: The implementation adds a bounded capability: generating required aliases to satisfy ClickHouse syntax requirements. The change is localized to hogql/resolver.py and guarded by new unit tests, matching tier 2 criteria. No broader systemic risk reduction or adoption metrics are demonstrated.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant for HogQL query execution against ClickHouse when subqueries or multiple joins require explicit names; could prevent silent failures or exceptions if the engine enforces strict aliasing.
review.uncertainty: Without access to live error reports or warehouse compatibility settings, it remains unclear how often missing aliases cause failures versus being optional.
